rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Master brand approach: both the company and its products are consistently referred to as Barco; no sub-branding or product logos. Use Barco as often as possible without adding division, market, or legal entity names unless the organizational structure truly matters.

rules.value: Use legal entity name
rules.channel: legal/contractual documents and address information fields
rules.note: The legal entity name is used only in materials and documents with legal implications; elsewhere use 'Barco'.

rules.value: Division/business unit names only combined with Barco plus a qualifier
rules.note: Division, business unit, or location names can only be used in combination with the Barco name and only if the org structure matters, always adding the qualifying word 'division,' 'business unit,' 'location,' or 'facility' (e.g. 'President of Barco's Entertainment division').

rules.value: Use Barco only, without division, market, or location
rules.channel: external communication material (brochures, ads, newsletters, magazines)
rules.note: e.g. 'Barco introduces new LED display.' Legal entity names appear only in the address information field.

rules.value: Division/business unit references allowed only in specific contexts, always qualified
rules.channel: investor, analyst, and general press communications
rules.note: References to divisions, business units, or locations must include the qualifying word 'division,' 'business unit,' 'location,' or 'facility.'

rules.value: Use Barco as often as possible
rules.note: Division/business unit/location names may be used only when qualified with 'division,' 'business unit,' 'location,' or 'facility.'

rules.value: Legal entity name in address field; Barco elsewhere in content
rules.channel: stationery and legally binding documents (invoices, letters, faxes, business cards, email signatures)
rules.note: Apart from the address information field, use Barco as often as possible in the body content.

rules.value: Visioneering a bright tomorrow
rules.note: Brand mantra used when communicating about Barco; written in lower case with a capital V.

rules.value: Visioneering Healthcare / Visioneering Enterprise / Visioneering Entertainment
rules.note: Standard terms used when referring to Barco's market segments.

rules.value: Inspirational 'What if' / 'Imagine' statements for segment-level messaging
rules.note: e.g. 'What if meetings could be truly inclusive?', 'Imagine diagnosing patients before they get sick,' 'What if you could perform surgery from the other side of the world?'

rules.value: Natural, everyday-speech writing style
rules.note: Avoid fancy oratorical touches, bureaucratic phrases, or explicit commercial wording; always write from an outcomes point of view that highlights the customer's benefit.

rules.value: Warm, open, personal tone
rules.note: Barco wants to be perceived as a warm, open company. Use a personal style with first- and second-person address (we/you) rather than the impersonal third person.

rules.value: Barco / the customer (used as impersonal third-person self-reference)
rules.note: Never refer to the company or the reader in the impersonal third person when a first- or second-person alternative is natural.

rules.value: colour
rules.note: American English (per Cambridge Dictionary) is the spelling standard for all Barco communication.

rules.value: grey
rules.note: American English (per Cambridge Dictionary) is the spelling standard for all Barco communication.

rules.value: visualisation
rules.note: American English (per Cambridge Dictionary) is the spelling standard for all Barco communication.

rules.value: centre
rules.note: American English (per Cambridge Dictionary) is the spelling standard for all Barco communication.

rules.value: programme
rules.note: American English (per Cambridge Dictionary) is the spelling standard for all Barco communication.

rules.value: Use active voice rather than passive
rules.note: Active sentences describe events more concisely and dynamically, e.g. 'A buys B' instead of 'B is bought by A.'

rules.value: Minimize jargon for general audiences
rules.note: Technical terms should only be used when addressing a specialist audience; if jargon is used in general texts (press releases, company intros, brochures), it must be explained on first use.

rules.value: Short words, simple sentences, well-structured paragraphs
rules.note: Use short, frequently-used words, minimize complicated constructions, aim for a maximum sentence length of 25 words, and treat paragraphs as units of thought. e.g. prefer 'We decided' over 'We made a decision.'

rules.value: Abbreviations spelled out in full on first appearance with the abbreviation in brackets
rules.note: Acronyms formed from initial letters are written in all capitals (e.g. NATO); abbreviations composed of word parts that can be pronounced as words are written as plain text (e.g. Unicef), unless the abbreviation is more commonly used than the full form.

rules.value: Numerals one to ten spelled in words; 11 upward (and decimals/fractions) written in figures
rules.note: Exceptions: page references and percentages are always in figures. Do: 'Two contracts,' 'Page 3,' '8%,' '24 displays.' Don't: '2 contracts,' 'Page three,' 'Eight percent,' 'Twenty-four displays.'

rules.value: Phone/fax format: +country code, area code, number
Dates written day/month/year
rules.note: Do: '3 June 2004,' 'June 3, 2003.' Don't: '3rd June 2003,' '3rd of June, 2003.'

rules.value: Currency symbol placed before the figure with no space; 'million' abbreviated to 'm', 'billion' always spelled out
rules.note: If the currency symbol is omitted, place the currency name after the figure. Do: '€250 million,' '€250m,' '€32 billion,' '32 billion euro.' Don't: '€ 250million,' '€250 m,' '€32 bn,' 'euro 32 billion.'

rules.value: Headlines: active voice, present tense, short (max two lines); initial cap only on first word of titles
rules.note: Example: 'Barco wins $25 million contract for LED installation at Leira stadium.'

rules.value: BARCO (written in full capitals)
rules.note: Barco is consistently written in lower case with a capital B; avoid full caps, including in copyright notices.

rules.value: Visioneering a bright tomorrow (lower case with capital V)
rules.note: The brand mantra is consistently written in lower case with a capital V.

rules.value: Copyright notice format: © [year], Barco
rules.note: Contains the copyright symbol ©, year of first publication, and owner, e.g. '© 2023, Barco.' Barco remains lower case with capital B.

rules.value: Product naming: descriptive name, compound word highlighting USP, or product code; precede name with Barco®
rules.note: e.g. Barco Canvas, ClickShare, Barco UniSee. Use only descriptive or compound names for key features. Exceptions require sign-off from Barco's brand manager.

rules.value: Only the Barco name and logo are trademarked; products/services get non-trademarked descriptive or compound names except in exceptional cases
rules.note: Exceptions include: 'crown jewel' products with high added value/revenue potential (e.g. UniSee); competitive reasons in markets with trademarked competitor offers (e.g. Demetra, Nexxis, Eonis); commercial/new-market potential (e.g. ClickShare); or trademarks inherited via acquisition (e.g. wePresent).

rules.value: Confident and future-facing
rules.note: Fan's personal impression (not an official style guide) that Barco's brand voice comes across as confident and future-facing. [chunk-19]

rules.value: Inspirational, uses big 'what if' style questions (e.g. 'what if surgery could happen from anywhere'), almost sci-fi at times
rules.note: Observed pattern in Barco marketing per fan blog draft; not confirmed official guidance. [chunk-19]

rules.value: visioneering
rules.note: Barco's own coined term (mashup of 'vision' + 'engineering') that they like to use in marketing, per fan observation. [chunk-19]

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Fan observes Barco tends to refer to itself simply as 'Barco' rather than using long corporate names for its divisions, except in investor-relations documents; interpreted as a 'one brand' approach rather than house-of-brands. [chunk-20]

rules.value: Use full/long corporate division names only in investor-relations documents
rules.note: Per fan's observation, division-specific corporate-speak names are reserved for investor-relations documents; elsewhere just 'Barco' is used. [chunk-20]

rules.value: Plain writing style, not flowery, short sentences, matter-of-fact
rules.note: Fan's read on Barco's writing style based on their marketing/press materials. [chunk-20]

rules.value: Not heavily jargon-laden, even when discussing technical products like projectors and LED walls
rules.note: Fan observation praising Barco for avoiding excessive jargon in technical content. [chunk-20]

rules.value: Inspirational, aspirational framing ("What if" statements, "Visioneering" language)
rules.note: Permitted for autumn/Q3 seasonal campaign copy, but must still adhere to the standard tone-of-voice rules.

rules.value: BARCO (full caps)
rules.note: Brand name should be written lower case with a capital B only; never use full caps, per capitalization section of the main guide.

rules.value: Bold
rules.note: One of Nike's two defining tone words per Tonelab's secondary analysis (no official Nike guide available).

rules.value: Motivational
rules.note: One of Nike's two defining tone words per Tonelab's secondary analysis (no official Nike guide available).

rules.value: Imperative, command-based language rather than descriptive statements
rules.note: Nike's language is imperative, built around commands rather than descriptions.

rules.value: Present tense delivery to create urgency and immediacy
rules.note: Copy is delivered in the present tense to create a sense of urgency and immediacy.

rules.value: Literal and direct expression, avoiding ambiguity, hedging, or tentative phrasing
rules.note: Expression is kept literal and direct, avoiding ambiguity, hedging, or tentative phrasing.

rules.value: Messaging built around 'Action vs. Excuse' tension, pushing reader from hesitation toward action
rules.note: Core framing of Nike's messaging; tagline 'Just Do It' cited as clearest distillation, challenging hesitation and pushing for immediate action over excuses.

rules.value: Empowers audience through movement and attitude rather than description
rules.note: Key voice principle drawn from the framework.

rules.value: Fosters urgency and personal responsibility
rules.note: Key voice principle drawn from the framework.

rules.value: Speaks to an audience that is 'ready to act' rather than persuading the reluctant
rules.note: Key voice principle drawn from the framework.

rules.value: Directly challenges excuses rather than soothing them
rules.note: Key voice principle drawn from the framework.

rules.value: Avoids passive voice
rules.note: Interpreted practice: Nike avoids passive voice in favor of dynamic, present-tense directives.

rules.value: Avoids soft qualifiers
rules.note: Interpreted practice: Nike avoids soft qualifiers in favor of dynamic, present-tense directives.

rules.value: Avoids delayed or tentative language
rules.note: Interpreted practice: Nike avoids delayed or tentative language, favoring dynamic, present-tense directives aimed at athletes and would-be athletes.
